title: Unit Converter - Length, Weight, Temp, Area & Speed
description: Instantly convert between metric and imperial units for length, weight, temperature, area, volume, and speed with high-precision factor tables.
quickAnswer: To convert between units, multiply the source value by the appropriate conversion factor. For length: 1 mile = 1.60934 km, 1 inch = 2.54 cm, 1 foot = 0.3048 m. For weight: 1 lb = 453.592 g, 1 kg = 2.20462 lb. For temperature: °C = (°F − 32) × 5 ÷ 9. All conversions run instantly in your browser using NIST-standard factor tables.

formula.title: Unit Conversion Formulas
formula.expression: Value in target unit = Value × Conversion factor
formula.explanation: Multiply by the exact conversion factor relative to the base SI unit (e.g. 1 meter = 3.28084 feet, 1 kilogram = 2.20462 pounds). For temperature, apply the linear formula: °F = (°C × 9/5) + 32 or °C = (°F − 32) × 5/9.

commonMistakes.title: Confusing US Liquid and Imperial Gallons
commonMistakes.description: A British (Imperial) gallon is 4.546 liters, while a US gallon is only 3.785 liters. Using the wrong gallon definition leads to a 20% measurement discrepancy.

commonMistakes.title: Applying Direct Factors to Temperatures
commonMistakes.description: You cannot multiply Fahrenheit by a single ratio because Fahrenheit and Celsius have different zero points (freezing is 32°F and 0°C). Always subtract 32 before scaling.

commonMistakes.title: Squaring Linear Conversion Factors for Area
commonMistakes.description: Since 1 yard = 3 feet, 1 square yard is not 3 square feet, but 3 × 3 = 9 square feet. Area factors square the linear relationship.

faqs.q: How are measurement conversions calculated accurately?
faqs.a: Non-temperature conversions normalize the source value to a fundamental SI base unit (like meters for length or kilograms for weight) using international NIST definitions, then divide by the target unit's exact conversion factor.

faqs.q: What is the formula to convert Celsius to Fahrenheit?
faqs.a: Multiply the Celsius temperature by 9/5 (or 1.8) and add 32: °F = (°C × 9/5) + 32. For example, 20°C converts to (20 × 1.8) + 32 = 68°F.

faqs.q: What is the formula to convert Fahrenheit to Celsius?
faqs.a: Subtract 32 from the Fahrenheit temperature, then multiply by 5/9: °C = (°F - 32) × 5/9. For instance, 98.6°F converts to (98.6 - 32) × 5/9 = 37°C.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a US gallon and an Imperial gallon?
faqs.a: A US liquid gallon is defined as exactly 231 cubic inches or approximately 3.78541 liters. An Imperial (British) gallon is defined as exactly 4.54609 liters, making the Imperial gallon approximately 20% larger than the US gallon.
Yes. By international agreement (the 1959 International Yard and Pound Agreement), 1 inch is defined as exactly 0.0254 meters, and 1 avoirdupois pound is defined as exactly 0.45359237 kilograms.

faqs.q: How many decimal places of precision are displayed?
faqs.a: Our unit converter displays high-precision floating-point values rounded to 6 decimal places for everyday physical units and 4 decimal places for temperatures, eliminating floating-point rounding errors.

faqs.q: Are any measurements or user inputs stored or uploaded?
faqs.a: No. All unit transformations occur entirely in your local browser using client-side JavaScript. No data is ever transmitted or logged.
